already-have.reason: Not implemented and not contradicted by any recorded owner decision. `secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:10-31` documents only F-20 per-position random start digits; `enter_pin()` (`cmd_request_unlock.rs:54`) returns the full 8-digit PIN to `gated_unlock` with no mid-entry SE query. A case-insensitive grep over `secure/src`, `docs/`, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and the memory directory for `anti-phish|security word|phishing word|prefix word|coldcard` finds no implementation, design note, or owner decision for or against prefix-derived words. GitHub search (`phishing`, `security words`, `Coldcard`, `PIN prefix`, `lookalike`, `swap`) returns only #601 (flash-resident personalised boot artifact, OPEN, design-first/owner-gated on a geometry page) and #249 (triple-UID attestation binding) as adjacent items; neither is an SE-bound CMAC-over-PIN-prefix check. The only recorded decisions nearby (`docs/security/production-security.md:161` boot-time anti-swap UID binding; `work-todo` archive item superseded by #22/#249) address MCU↔SE binding verified by firmware, not a user-verifiable pre-PIN signal, so IMP-10 is complementary rather than conflicting.
already-have.corrections: (1) Tracking: no open issue covers this; it should be filed as a new issue cross-linked to #601 (and #249), and the design belongs as an amendment to the existing `docs/security/user-device-verification.md` (the file #601's triage names as the amend-not-duplicate target), not a new doc. (2) Scope honesty: the words are SE-bound, so they detect WHOLE-DEVICE substitution only. `docs/verification/hardware-assumption-boundary-2026-07-17.md:800-830` records the evil-maid case where the attacker keeps the user's own SEs and replaces MCU firmware (Donjon Safe 3 shape): a trojan MCU image on the user's original unit would still obtain the correct CMAC from the user's SE050 and print the correct words, so IMP-10 does not close that branch — state it explicitly in the proposal. (3) Rate-limit location: the repo's SE050 driver uses UserID auth and SCP03 (`secure/src/se050/`), and the OPTIGA side already uses an HMAC-verify against F1D0 that auto-increments the attempt counter (`secure/src/optiga/mod.rs:1343-1348`), which is exactly the counter the proposal must NOT touch; SE050 has no native per-query throttle on a plain symmetric-key object, so the "rate limit in silicon" claim needs a concrete mechanism (e.g. a dedicated SE050 UserID/policy-gated key or a separate OPTIGA counter object) before it can be stated as a property. (4) Existing `duress-pin` feature (`secure/src/dual_se.rs:228-290`, provisioned and unlocked on both SEs) must be considered: the duress PIN's 4-digit prefix yields different words unless designed to share the prefix or to learn a second pair, and the words must not reveal which PIN is being typed. (5) Available building blocks confirmed: `secure/src/ui/secret_text.rs` exists for constant-time rendering; `optiga::hmac_sha256` helper exists (`optiga/mod.rs:921`). Nothing checked refutes the item.

feasible.reason: The proposal is realisable on pq1 as pure firmware (kind=firmware is right, cost M / P2 are reasonable) and it does raise the bar against a lookalike-device swap, so it is not refuted outright. But it is over-claimed on three points that must be corrected before it is banked. (1) Scope: against the threat text's own second case, "a genuine one with an implant and a cloned shell", the words provide ZERO protection: the implant sits on a device whose SE/DHUK is genuine, so the words are correct and the implant harvests the full PIN exactly as before. Only a different-silicon substitution is covered. (2) It raises cost, does not prevent: in an evil-maid swap the attacker by construction holds the genuine unit, so (a) a live relay (trojan sends the 4-digit prefix out, attacker keys it into the genuine device, words come back) fits comfortably inside the proposed ~2 s query budget and is undetectable, and (b) offline table-building over a FIXED 4-digit prefix is 10^4 queries ≈ 5.6 h at 2 s/query (≈14–28 h if driven through the two-button trusted UI with a button robot and ~7 s re-boot per power cycle) — well inside the window before a victim's next use. Coldcard's residual is the same but its 2–6 digit, length-hidden prefix makes the table 100× larger; pq1's fixed PIN_LEN=8 / 4-digit prefix (proto/src/lib.rs:21, secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs) is the weak form. (3) "Rate limit must live in the SE (one query per ~2 s)" is unrealisable as written: neither the SE050 nor OPTIGA Trust M has a clock; the only silicon limits are COUNT-based (SE050 UserID maxAttempts / counter objects, OPTIGA LUC E120–E123), and a lifetime count cannot distinguish an enumerating attacker from months of normal unlocks without bricking usability. A time delay has to be MCU-enforced — which is acceptable here precisely because RDP-2 plus the PIN-gated fw-update path means the genuine-device enumerator can only drive the trusted UI, but with no battery nothing persists across a power cut, so the real floor is "per-boot query cap × ~7 s boot", not 2 s. Driver facts also differ from the proposal: the SE050 driver has no in-SE MAC command at all (secure/src/se050/scp03.rs only does host-side SCP03 CMAC), and creating a dedicated key object at first boot lands inside the production-quarantined first-boot / S-5..S-7 object-layout ceremony; the OPTIGA driver already drives DecryptSym HMAC-verify (PARAM_HMAC_MODE=0x20, LUC-bound, secure/src/optiga/apdu.rs:160-172, 902-940) but EncryptSym HMAC-generate (0x94) is absent and a new pre-shared-secret OID is another irreversible metadata ceremony in S-1 territory. The cheapest sound realisation needs no SE change at all: SAES-CMAC(DHUK) over a domain-separated prefix via the existing `hw::saes_cmac::cmac_dhuk` (secure/src/hw/saes_cmac.rs:44) — per-die, final only after the RDP-2 self-lock, not in flash — which satisfies the stated rationale ("bind to a per-device secret a trojan cannot precompute") without touching either SE.
feasible.corrections: 1. Narrow the threat: covers only whole-device substitution with different silicon; explicitly state it does NOT cover an implant in the user's genuine device (words will match) — that case belongs to IMP-03/mesh/attestation, not here. 2. State the residual honestly: a networked trojan with a live relay to the genuine unit, or an attacker who pre-enumerates the prefix table, passes; the feature forces the attacker to hold the genuine unit AND either relay or spend hours — it is a cost raise, as on Coldcard. 3. Replace the fixed 4-digit prefix with a user-chosen, length-hidden prefix (2–6 digits, Coldcard-style; the F-20 digit scrambler and the 2-button UI can tolerate a 'show words now' long-press), and add a per-boot query cap (e.g. 2 word-queries per power cycle, then full PIN required) so the enumeration floor becomes ~10^4..10^6 × ≥7 s rather than 2 s. 4. Drop 'rate limit in the SE'; neither SE can rate-limit by time. If an SE binding is still wanted, the only count-based lever is an OPTIGA LUC on a new pre-shared-secret OID via EncryptSym HMAC-generate (needs the 0x94 APDU plus an irreversible metadata ceremony → S-1 gate); the SE050 route needs a new HMAC key object + MACOneShot support and a first-boot object creation step inside the quarantined rdp2-self-lock flow. Prefer SAES-CMAC(DHUK) via `cmac_dhuk` with a domain tag (e.g. "pq1-pin-words-v1" || prefix_len || prefix); the words only become stable after the RDP-2 self-lock (DHUK is final only then), so the wizard 'learn your words' step must run post-lock — on first field boot that ordering already holds. 5. Wording: the prefix does not stay 'in S-world in clear' if sent to an SE — it crosses I2C encrypted under SCP03/shield, which is no worse than today's SE050 PIN path; with the DHUK route it never leaves the MCU. 6. Duress interaction: the duress AuthRef (F1D8) means a duress PIN must yield equally plausible words (same function, never a 'wrong' marker) and the user must learn both pairs. 7. Rendering through `secret_text` is fine but mostly cosmetic: the words are shown to the user and reveal only the prefix equivalence class; what matters is that word derivation is constant-time w.r.t. the prefix (CMAC is). 8. Flash: the BIP-39 wordlist is already linked (measured_boot), so incremental cost is ~1–3 KB; irrelevant to the 76,949 B ui-px overrun but must be counted. 9. Complementarity with #601 is real and stronger than stated: because the words are DERIVED, this needs no stored artifact and sidesteps #601's no-free-page storage blocker. 10. Keep off-by-default with a wizard step; add a 'forgot words' recovery = full PIN still works (words are advisory), which also means a user who ignores a wrong pair gets no protection — UX must make the stop condition loud.

vendor-claim.reason: The core precedent and novelty claims hold: Coldcard demonstrably ships anti-phishing words (present in the first public commit of the bootloader, July 2018 = Mk1 era) computed by an SE HMAC over a hashed PIN prefix, Foundation ships 'Security Words' off-by-default after 4 digits, and neither Trezor (grep of /home/nicola/repos/trezor-firmware: zero hits) nor Ledger ships an equivalent, so novelty='parity' is correct. Two details in vendor_precedent/rationale are wrong or misleading and the proposal's rate-limit design has NO vendor precedent: (1) Coldcard's '2 s rate limit' is not an SE policy — in 2018 it was an MCU bootloader delay_ms(150/2500) plus an MCU-side lookup counter capped at 25; in current Mk4 code there is no timer at all, the delay is an artifact of 12 chained ATECC608 HMAC iterations each needing a software-SHA pair-unlock (~8 ms each), with pin_delay() compiled out; the SE itself enforces nothing time-based. (2) Foundation did not 'add' Security Words in Passport Prime — the original Passport (Core) already shipped them with identical semantics. Additionally, SE050 has no time-based rate-limit policy (plug-and-trust policy enum has no rate/throttle bit) and OPTIGA E120 LUC is a usage-count cap, so the IMP's 'rate limit must live in the SE' requirement is novel relative to every vendor and needs a design that does not exist off-the-shelf. The 35c3 source is about server SPI-bus implants and supports only the threat framing, not the precedent.
vendor-claim.corrections: vendor_precedent should read: 'Coldcard anti-phishing words since the original 2018 Coldcard (Mk1/Mk2, ATECC508A; pin_prefix_words() present in the first public commit 9f04ac1, 2018-07-24): prefix -> double-SHA256(pairing_secret||purpose||prefix||otp_key) -> HMAC in SE1 under a per-device key the MCU never holds (KEYNUM_words in 2018; KEYNUM_pin_stretch via ae_stretch_iter(KDF_ITER_WORDS=12) on Mk4/ATECC608) -> 32-bit result, 22 bits shown as two BIP-39 words. Rate limiting was MCU-bootloader-side in 2018 (delay_ms 150 ms, 2500 ms after 10 lookups, plus a lookup counter that INCONSISTENT()s past 25) and on Mk4 is only the ~2 s compute/bus cost of 12 chained SE HMACs — there is no SE-enforced timer or policy. Foundation Passport (original Passport Core, pre-Prime) ships Security Words disabled by default, shown after the first 4 PIN digits; Passport Prime inherits the same feature (docs.foundation.xyz/passport/advanced and /prime/prime-apps/settings/general/). Trezor: none (no anti-phishing/security-word code in trezor-firmware; its swap mitigations are companion-side AuthenticateDevice attestation core/src/apps/management/authenticate_device.py:9 and a custom homescreen core/src/apps/management/apply_settings.py:19). Ledger: none (Stax/Flex custom lock-screen image is cosmetic/copyable; Genuine Check is companion-side).' Proposal corrections: SE050 object policies (POLICY_OBJ_*) contain no rate-limit/time policy, so 'one query per ~2 s enforced by SE050 policy' is not achievable as stated; achievable SE-side shapes are (a) an OPTIGA usage-count (LUC, E120-style) cap on the HMAC key — a lifetime budget, not a rate, or (b) Coldcard-style cost-based limiting via many chained SE MAC calls (SE050 MACOneShot_G with CMAC_128/HMAC_SHA256 under SCP03) — which is compute-time, not policy. Note Coldcard's own 2018 code DID consume a counter for word lookups (25 cap), contradicting the IMP's 'separate from the PIN attempt counter so it cannot burn attempts' as a precedent point — that separation is PQ1's own design choice. Sources: replace 35c3 'Modchips of the State' (server/BMC SPI implant talk, no hardware-wallet content) with the Coldcard bootloader source (github.com/Coldcard/firmware stm32/bootloader/pins.c and ae.c) and docs.foundation.xyz/passport/advanced. The rationale's 'since Mk1' is supported; 'Foundation added in Passport Prime' is not.
